title: Nasal [ɑ̃] — an, am, en, em (set 7)
focus: These spellings all make the nasal vowel [ɑ̃], as in « enfant ». In Québec it is usually pronounced further forward in the mouth than in Paris, so it can sound close to a Parisian « in » — listen for that. Careful: the verb ending -ent (« ils chantent ») is silent, never nasal, and a following vowel or doubled n/m cancels the nasal (« banane », « Jeanne »). Careful: « chien » is written with -en but says [jɛ̃], like « bien » and « rien » — not this sound.

sentences.fr: Cette fin de semaine, nous allons à la c[am]pagne.
sentences.en: This weekend, we're going to the countryside.

sentences.fr: Mon oncle a une maison au milieu des ch[am]ps.
sentences.en: My uncle has a house in the middle of the fields.

sentences.fr: Il y a des vaches, des moutons et un gr[an]d chien.
sentences.en: There are cows, sheep and a big dog.
In the evening, we eat together outside.

sentences.fr: C'est calme et le t[em]ps passe l[en]tem[en]t.
sentences.en: It's calm and time passes slowly.
